**Recursion check.** Let P(n) be the probability that two specific players ever share a battle when n players remain. Among the C(n,4) possible groups:
- Both selected: 12/(n(n−1)). They battle, so this contributes 12/(n(n−1)).
- Exactly one selected: 8(n−4)/(n(n−1)). That player must win (probability 1/4) for both to survive, so this contributes 2(n−4)/(n(n−1))·P(n−3).
- Neither selected: (n−4)(n−5)/(n(n−1)). Both survive, contributing (n−4)(n−5)/(n(n−1))·P(n−3).

Combining the last two terms gives P(n−3) with coefficient (n−4)(n−3)/(n(n−1)), so

P(n) = 12/(n(n−1)) + (n−4)(n−3)/(n(n−1)) · P(n−3), with P(4) = 1.

**Closed form.** Try P(n) = 4/n. The recursion holds: 12/(n(n−1)) + 4(n−4)/(n(n−1)) = (4n−4)/(n(n−1)) = 4/n. The base case P(4) = 1 matches. So P(34) = 4/34 = 2/17.
